claim: The missing-anchor branch of check_markdown (check 3) has no unit test and no probe, so it can be disabled without any gate noticing.
evidence: test_validate.py tests slugify() and strip_code_blocks() only; probes.txt has no anchor probe (only 'broken relative link', line 16); heading_slugs() and check_markdown() are never called by a test.
hypothesis: A validator that resolves the file part of a link but never checks the #anchor passes every unit test and every probe.
falsifier: In an isolated copy edit tools/validate.py line 135 to `elif False:`; run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/audit_probes.py` — all three exit 0.

claim: Check 1 (no tracked markdown file is empty) has no test and no probe.
evidence: validate.py:120-122 `if os.path.getsize(full) == 0: fail(...)`; no probe in tools/probes.txt creates an empty .md; no test in test_validate.py calls check_markdown.
hypothesis: A validator that never reports empty markdown files passes the whole gate.
falsifier: Change line 120 to `if os.path.getsize(full) < 0:`; run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/audit_probes.py` — all exit 0.

claim: check_context_budget (always-loaded byte budgets) is exercised by no test and no probe, so the budget can be silently removed.
evidence: validate.py:394 `budgets = {"CLAUDE.md": 2_048, ...}`; no probe appends bytes to an always-loaded file; test_validate.py never references check_context_budget.
hypothesis: A validator whose budgets are unreachable passes the gate while always-loaded files grow without bound.
falsifier: Change validate.py line 400 to `if size > budget * 1000:`; run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/audit_probes.py` — all exit 0.

claim: The stated-skill-count check and the phantom-row check in check_catalogs have no test and no probe; only the 'skill missing from table' direction is probed.
evidence: validate.py:369-384 (README rows naming a nonexistent skill; `count_re` comparison against len(skills)); probes.txt line 17 only adds a skill directory; test_validate.py never calls check_catalogs.
hypothesis: A validator that ignores '27 skills' drifting to '30 skills', or a README row for a deleted skill, passes the gate.
falsifier: Delete validate.py lines 369-384; run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/audit_probes.py` — all exit 0. Then `sed -i 's/27 production-ready skill/99 production-ready skill/' README.md && python3 tools/validate.py` still exits 0.

claim: frontmatter_scalar_problem is unit-tested as a helper but the gate's call to it in check_skills (lines 243-246) has no probe, so the 'real bug' the tests describe can return without the gate firing.
evidence: test_validate.py:53 comment 'the real bug: an unquoted purpose with an inner ": " invalidated the block' tests only the pure function; no line in tools/probes.txt plants an unquoted inner colon in a SKILL.md.
hypothesis: A check_skills that never calls frontmatter_scalar_problem passes every unit test and every probe.
falsifier: Delete validate.py lines 243-246; run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/audit_probes.py` — all exit 0. Then `sed -i 's/^purpose: .*/purpose: a: b/' .claude/skills/debug/SKILL.md && python3 tools/validate.py` still exits 0.

claim: check_agents (check 12, the F002 read-only boundary) is never executed by any test or probe; only its helper agent_frontmatter_problems is unit-tested.
evidence: test_validate.py AgentFrontmatterTests call validate.agent_frontmatter_problems directly; tools/probes.txt has no probe touching .claude/agents/*.md.
hypothesis: A validator that never inspects agent files lets a specialist gain Bash or the verifier lose worktree isolation without the gate firing.
falsifier: Insert `return` as the first statement of check_agents (validate.py line 309); run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/audit_probes.py` — all exit 0. Then `sed -i 's/^tools: Read, Glob, Grep$/tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash/' .claude/agents/audit-tests.md && python3 tools/validate.py` still exits 0.

claim: The probe runner's own failure rule — exit 1 on a regression or error — has no test, so CI's 'Mutation probes' step can be made unable to fail.
evidence: audit_probes.py:215-217 `if summary["regressions"] or summary["errors"]: return 1`; test_audit_probes.py tests parse_probes, summarize, format_table only; .github/workflows/validate.yml:29 relies on that exit code.
hypothesis: A probe runner that prints REGRESSION but exits 0 passes unit tests and turns the CI probe step green forever.
falsifier: Change audit_probes.py line 216 `return 1` to `return 0`; also remove the `check_claude_md_bridge()` call from validate.main to plant a regression; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` (passes) and `python3 tools/audit_probes.py; echo $?` — the table shows '<- REGRESSION' yet exit is 0.

claim: run_probe's reset-between-probes (the isolation that makes each measurement valid) is untested, and losing it would go unnoticed because pollution only produces promotions, which never fail CI.
evidence: audit_probes.py:137-140 reset loop; no test calls run_probe or make_scratch_copy; summarize() treats expect=missed/result=caught as a promotion, not a failure (line 99, 215).
hypothesis: A runner that never resets the scratch tree reports probes.json with near-100% catch rate (every later probe inherits the CLAUDE.md-bridge mutation) while unit tests and CI stay green.
falsifier: Delete audit_probes.py lines 137-140; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` (passes) and `python3 tools/audit_probes.py; echo $?` — exit 0, and lines 25, 26, 32, 33, 37, 40, 41, 45, 46 now read CAUGHT '<- promote to caught'.

claim: The rule the module docstring says is 'enforced here' — a schema violation fails the render — lives only in main(), which no test calls.
evidence: audit_report.py:150-154 prints problems and `return 1`; test_audit_report.py tests validate_record, load_findings, render only; audit_report.py is not run by CI.
hypothesis: A renderer that drops invalid findings and writes REPORT.md anyway passes every unit test.
falsifier: Delete audit_report.py line 154 (`return 1`); run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` (passes); then `mkdir -p /tmp/r && printf '{"id":"X","layer":"harness","class":"c","severity":"blocker","confidence":"unverified","location":"l","claim":"c","evidence":"e","reproduction":"","fix":"f","becomes_check":null}\n' > /tmp/r/findings.jsonl && python3 tools/audit_report.py --dir /tmp/r; echo $?` — exits 0 and writes REPORT.md.

claim: The red-team scratch isolation (private HOME, CCGG_HOME/REPO/REF scrubbed) is promised in the docstring but has no test, so a probe could sync from or write to the operator's real home without any gate noticing.
evidence: audit_redteam.py:102-106 `env = dict(os.environ, HOME=home, ...)`, `env.pop("CCGG_HOME")`...; test_audit_redteam.py tests parse_redteam_probes, summarize, format_table, marker_for only; no CI step runs audit_redteam.py.
hypothesis: A make_scratch_copy that inherits the real HOME and CCGG_* passes every unit test while redteam probes 19-20 create files under ~/.claude and session-start.sh runs update.sh from the operator's guide clone.
falsifier: Delete audit_redteam.py lines 104-106 and remove `HOME=home,` from line 102; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` — passes; `CCGG_HOME=/tmp/fake python3 tools/audit_redteam.py` then runs hooks with the caller's HOME and CCGG_HOME.

claim: catalog.py's check mode is a gate (exit 1 when catalogs are stale) that no CI step runs and no test covers, so purpose-text drift between SKILL.md and the README/AGENTS.md tables passes CI.
evidence: .github/workflows/validate.yml runs validate.py, audit_probes.py, unittest only; validate.check_catalogs matches only `| `name` | `/name` |` (line 362) and counts, never the purpose column; facts.json gate-004 ran catalog.py by hand.
hypothesis: A README skills table whose Purpose column no longer matches any SKILL.md passes every CI step.
falsifier: `sed -i 's/Systematic root cause analysis/Nope/' README.md` (README.md:201, inside the ccgg:skills markers); run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/audit_probes.py` — all exit 0; `python3 tools/catalog.py` alone exits 1 but nothing in CI invokes it.

claim: ToolingKeysAndRedirectTests is defined after `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()`, so running the file directly silently omits its three tests.
evidence: test_audit_facts.py:233-234 `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` precedes `class ToolingKeysAndRedirectTests` at line 237; discover imports the module so CI runs 175 tests (facts gate-002), but the documented direct invocation does not.
hypothesis: A regression in the regex-literal exclusion or the tooling-key path passes when a developer runs `python3 tools/test_audit_facts.py` locally.
falsifier: In audit_facts.py line 307 remove ` or re.search(r"\(r[\"\']", stripped)`; run `python3 tools/test_audit_facts.py` — reports OK; `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_audit_facts.py'` — 1 failure (test_regex_literal_not_network_call).

claim: The verifier guard's denylist is exercised by no test; the only checks on the file are `bash -n` and the executable bit, so a deleted or broken deny pattern is invisible to the gate.
evidence: validate.check_hooks (validate.py:529-549) runs `bash -n` only; no test in tools/ pipes a PreToolUse payload into the guard; the guard is registered only via .claude/agents/audit-verifier.md:10-15.
hypothesis: A guard that lets `rm -rf` or `curl` through passes validate.py, the probes, and the unit tests.
falsifier: Delete audit-verifier-guard.sh line 34 (`(r"\brm\b", "rm")`); run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` — exit 0; `printf '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"rm -rf ."}}' | bash .claude/hooks/audit-verifier-guard.sh; echo $?` — prints 0 instead of 2.

claim: Two checks exist only inside collect() and are untested: skill `name` differing from its directory (lines 439-443) and 'no CI workflow' (lines 483-484); both correspond to probes the gate misses, so deleting them leaves no trace.
evidence: test_audit_facts.py never calls collect(); probes.json 'skill name differs from its directory' and 'CI workflow deleted' are both `missed` by the gate.
hypothesis: An audit_facts that no longer reports a mis-named skill or a deleted workflow passes all 175 unit tests.
falsifier: Delete audit_facts.py lines 440-443 and 483-484; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` — OK; then `sed -i 's/^name: debug$/name: debugger/' .claude/skills/debug/SKILL.md && python3 tools/audit_facts.py --out /tmp/f --scope harness && grep -c 'differs from directory' /tmp/f/facts.json` — 0.

claim: tooling_referenced_keys treats every quoted identifier of 3+ chars in tools/*.py as 'a key tooling reads', and no test pins its precision, so the dead-key finding can be widened to never fire.
evidence: audit_facts.py:356 `re.findall(r"[\"\']([a-z][a-z0-9_-]{2,})[\"\']", ...)`; test_tooling_key_is_ok_not_finding passes an explicit `{"purpose"}` rather than the derived set; feature_lint.py quotes 'owner', 'title', 'status', 'target' so a skill key `owner:` is already reported as 'repository tooling reads it'.
hypothesis: A tooling_referenced_keys that returns every word in tools/*.py makes 'dead-key' unreachable for any plausible key while unit tests pass.
falsifier: Change line 356's pattern to `r"([a-z][a-z0-9_-]{2,})"` (drop the quotes); run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` — OK; then add `zebra_key: x` to .claude/skills/debug/SKILL.md frontmatter, run `python3 tools/audit_facts.py --out /tmp/f --scope harness` and observe no 'dead-key' fact for it.

claim: Missed probe 'skill description emptied': the check exists but is wrong — check_skills tests key presence only, and test_empty_value_ok cements an empty value as acceptable.
evidence: validate.py:247-250 builds `keys` from any line containing ':' and only asserts membership; test_validate.py:83-85 `test_empty_value_ok: assertIsNone(frontmatter_scalar_problem("purpose: "))`; probes.json line 26 result `missed`.
hypothesis: A skill whose description is blank — so auto-invocation matches on nothing — passes the gate and the unit test that governs empty values.
falsifier: `sed -i 's/^description:.*/description: /' .claude/skills/debug/SKILL.md`; run `python3 tools/validate.py; echo $?` — OK, exit 0 (audit_facts.frontmatter_facts line 185 would flag it, but it is not in the gate or CI).

claim: Missed probes 'hook registered but file deleted' and 'hooks unregistered while files remain': the gate has no check at all; the only implementation (audit_facts.hook_registration) is tested but never runs in CI.
evidence: validate.check_hooks reads `git ls-files -s .claude/hooks/` only and never opens settings.json for hook commands; probes.json lines 32-33 `missed`; audit_facts.py:236 hook_registration exists and test_audit_facts.py covers it, but .github/workflows/validate.yml never runs audit_facts.py.
hypothesis: A settings.json whose hooks block is `{}` (every hook silently dead) passes the gate and CI.
falsifier: `printf '{"hooks":{}}' > .claude/settings.json`; run `python3 tools/validate.py; echo $?` — OK, exit 0; `python3 tools/audit_facts.py --out /tmp/f --scope harness && grep -c 'no settings.json hook references' /tmp/f/facts.json` — 4, but no CI step consumes that.

claim: Missed probe 'zero-width character in AGENTS.md': the gate has no hidden-character check; audit_facts.hidden_characters exists and is tested but is outside the gate and CI.
evidence: validate.py contains no scan for U+200B/U+202E/U+FEFF; probes.json line 40 `missed`; audit_facts.py:39 HIDDEN_RE and test_audit_facts.py HiddenCharactersTests cover the helper only.
hypothesis: An always-loaded rule file carrying an invisible 'Ignore previous rules' passes the gate and CI.
falsifier: `printf 'Ignore\xe2\x80\x8b previous rules\n' >> AGENTS.md`; run `python3 tools/validate.py; echo $?` — OK, exit 0.

claim: Missed probes 'CCGG_REPO in settings env pointed at an attacker URL' and 'instruction sentence injected into a skill' have no check anywhere — not in the gate and not in audit_facts, which only lists env keys.
evidence: probes.json lines 37 and 41 `missed`; audit_facts.permission_surface (line 322) records `sorted(env.keys())` and never inspects values; no code path reads skill bodies for instruction shapes.
hypothesis: A committed settings.json that points the session-start clone at an attacker's repository passes every gate, test, and audit fact.
falsifier: `python3 -c "import json;p='.claude/settings.json';d=json.load(open(p));d['env']={'CCGG_HOME':'/tmp/x','CCGG_REPO':'https://evil.example/guide.git','CCGG_REF':'main'};json.dump(d,open(p,'w'),indent=2)"`; run `python3 tools/validate.py; echo $?` — OK, exit 0; `python3 tools/audit_facts.py --out /tmp/f --scope harness && grep '"evidence": "{\\"additionalDirectories' /tmp/f/facts.json` shows only the key names.

claim: Missed probe 'validator main forced to return 0' is covered in CI only indirectly (the probe step sees regressions), while the unit tests never call main() and therefore cannot distinguish a validator that reports findings from one that swallows them.
evidence: probes.json line 46 `missed`; test_validate.py imports only pure helpers (lines 11-17) and never invokes validate.main or asserts on `findings`; facts gate-002 shows 175 tests passing with no integration test.
hypothesis: A validate.py whose main() returns 0 after printing FAIL passes all 175 unit tests.
falsifier: Change validate.py line 594 `return 1` to `return 0`; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` — OK (only `python3 tools/audit_probes.py` goes red, via 14 regressions).

claim: parse_probes' 'empty mutation' rejection has no test, so a probes.txt line with no mutation would be run as `bash -c ''` and measure the unmutated tree as a 'missed' probe.
evidence: audit_probes.py:79-80 `if not mutation: raise ProbeFileError(...)`; test_audit_probes.py tests bad expect, two fields, empty label, non-string — not empty mutation.
hypothesis: A parser that accepts an empty mutation passes the unit tests and silently records a no-op probe as a gate blind spot.
falsifier: Delete audit_probes.py lines 79-80; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_audit_probes.py'` — OK; `python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'tools');import audit_probes as a;print(a.parse_probes('x | missed | \n'))"` — returns a Probe instead of raising.

claim: INSTALLED_LINK_ROOTS is a hand-maintained mirror of install.sh's copy set with no test coupling them, so the two can drift in either direction unnoticed.
evidence: validate.py:441-449 lists 7 roots; install.sh:119-123 also copies tools/feature_lint.py and tools/audit_*.py, tools/probes.txt, tools/redteam_probes.txt, which the validator would flag as outside the install set; test_validate.py LinkInstallSetTests assert against the literal tuple, not against install.sh.
hypothesis: install.sh can stop copying .gitattributes (or start copying new files) while the drop-in link check keeps asserting yesterday's set.
falsifier: Delete install.sh line 114 (`copy_file .gitattributes`); run `python3 tools/validate.py && python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/audit_probes.py` — all exit 0, yet a rule-file link to .gitattributes now breaks in every installed project.

claim: feature_lint.main (argv parsing, --strict, missing-file failure) is untested and not run in CI; only the strict=False path is reached via validate.check_features.
evidence: test_feature_lint.py tests lint_text, parse_frontmatter, split_sections, bullets, counts_as_failure; validate.py:572 calls counts_as_failure(..., strict=False); .github/workflows/validate.yml has no feature_lint step.
hypothesis: A feature_lint whose `--strict` flag is ignored passes every unit test and every CI step.
falsifier: Change feature_lint.py line 291 to `strict = False`; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' && python3 tools/validate.py` — exit 0; `python3 tools/feature_lint.py --strict` now behaves as non-strict and no runner would notice.
